title: FREE Bodybuilding Split (Olympic Weightlifter Physique edition)
summary: NH walks through two free 3-4 day full-body programs for an Olympic weightlifter physique: a pure bodybuilding version using only dehybridized patterns, and a hybrid version with bastardized Oly variations (hang/power cleans, push press, snatch-grip work, 'Toshiki raises'). He explains exercise order by importance, supersets and giant sets, Saturday as the expendable day, and why shoulders, traps, upper back, quads and abs are prioritised.
claims: The pure bodybuilding program contains no Oly lift technique at all, only plain compounds and isolation, so its technical rating is very low
The hybrid program applies both dehybridization and bastardization, keeping clean and snatch variations but never the full lifts
Start Monday with overhead press 3-5 sets of 3-7 reps; the wide range allows volume and intensity manipulation (e.g. 3x3 for intensity, 5x4-7 for volume)
Superset OHP with shrugs 3-5x10-15: after pressing, lower the bar, add plates and shrug, since your shrug strength far exceeds your press strength
The overhead press and the bench are the lifts he most supports supersetting because the paired exercise won't damage their performance
Rest about three minutes after each OHP/shrug superset round
Squats 3x3-5 kept low volume and relatively high intensity, partly to preserve the spirit of Olympic lifting and partly to avoid cardiovascular exhaustion after the first superset
A full-body template is required for the Oly physique; an upper/lower doesn't cut it and push/pull/legs is not enough lower-body volume
Lateral raises 3x8-12 are the last shoulder exercise on Monday, more would be overkill
Order exercises by importance: the ones lowest in the day get skipped most often, so put the least important tonnage last
Saturday is the least important day; if you can only train three days, skip Saturday
Dumbbell or seal rows 4x8-12 give upper-back volume without taxing a posterior chain already loaded by squats
Chinese lifters do dumbbell rows standing, unsupported, braced with the core, no bench
Dumbbell curls 4x6-12 are the only direct biceps isolation because Oly lifters don't have the biggest biceps
Train abs directly every day; if you skip core you will never have the six-pack that defines the Chinese weightlifter look
If you must skip the last block, move the ab exercise earlier into the first superset rather than dropping it
Deadlift 1-3 sets of 3-5; beginners at manipulating ranges should just do the simplest form, one set of five
After every deadlift set, warm-ups included, do single-leg calf raises to failure
Weighted push-ups 3x4-8, weighted chin-ups 3x3-5 and hanging knee raises 3xAMRAP; bench press is fine but felt out of place in an Oly program
If you can't yet do weighted chin-ups you should probably run a novice program first, unless you are a heavier individual
Backhand triceps extensions (like a tennis backhand) have the best injury-prevention profile given all the vertical pressing
Neck, hamstrings/glutes and triceps finishers are done for high reps (15-20, 10-15, 10-20) because these muscles respond well and to balance heavy, low-pump compounds
If you skip neck work all the time you'll have a pencil neck
Weighted dips 3x3-5 on Friday keep strength up without overdoing the chest; lean more upright for triceps
Upright rows are not inherently dangerous; find a pain-free implement (EZ bar, dumbbells, kettlebell, band) and progressively overload
Exercises higher on the 'totem of danger' should be done in higher rep ranges to reduce injury risk
Goblet squats 4x8-12 for quad volume; paused squats work in the same range but are torture
Seated DB overhead press 4x6-12 after dips and upright rows may be overkill for some; substitute diamond/handstand push-ups or skip until shoulders are conditioned
Two vertical pushes a week are essential for big round shoulders, and the shoulders must be conditioned to handle it
Bent-over lateral raises 4x10-15 because heavy pressing makes rear-delt development essential; a weak rear delt makes the whole shoulder weak
French press 3x6-10 once a week for the triceps long head, which Oly lifters tend to lack
Oly lifters' forearms look good mostly because they are lean; forearm isolation once a week with finger curls is enough
Saturday: RDLs 4x8-12 and weighted pull-ups 4x3-5, farmer's carries 3xAMRAP for traps, unweighted reverse rows and banded face pulls for blood flow
Face pulls should be done with a band or very light weight, just to send blood to the rear delts
Do the last superset/giant set of each day with zero rest, otherwise giant sets become time devouring; other supersets take 3-4 minutes rest
The pure program runs three to four times a week
Behind-the-head snatch-grip press is an Oly hypertrophy variation but very mobility-demanding; never go heavy if unconditioned
Hang cleans or hang power cleans 3-5x6-10 replace shrugs to add trap stretch and posterior chain work
The hybrid program is tougher on conditioning and recovery but not necessarily better for hypertrophy
Lu raises (Lu Xiaojun lateral raise variation) 3x8-12, start very light because of shoulder mobility demands
'Toshiki raises', copied from Toshiki Yamamoto, are a snatch-grip hang pull finished with a calf raise, an explosive trap/shoulder/calf movement supersetted with deadlifts
Alternate between push-ups and dips for horizontal pressing for injury prevention
On ring knee raises hold a full squeezed chin-up position, not arms extended, to keep a packed upper back
Front squats are better done in lower rep ranges, so they're programmed 4x4-6
Push press 4x4-8 after front squats; this combo is advanced and wrecks abs and cardio
For behind-the-head supinated triceps extensions, use a band anchored behind you if gravity-loaded versions stress the shoulders
The hybrid program expects the upper back to fully recover in 48 hours, so reverse rows are weighted at 3x6-10
Shoulders won't turn into planets in a week; stay injury-free, don't push through pain
Neither program will make you good at Oly lifting; to add strength, drop Saturday and add a snatch day and a clean and jerk day, or do AM strength/PM hypertrophy sessions if advanced

standing braced Chinese style, no bench
